t: Section 1 of the Act of August 3, 1950, chapter 537, as amended (10 U.S.C. 3201 note), is amended by striking out “July 1, 1971” and inserting in place thereof “July 1, 1973”.

fable.w: This section only extends a date in an existing statute by substituting one date for another. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by striking out “July 1, 1971” and inserting in place thereof “July 1, 1973”

opus.w: This section only changes a date in an earlier Act, replacing "July 1, 1971" with "July 1, 1973". Someone might be tempted to read participation into the underlying Act it amends. But nothing in this text involves a party outside the federal government taking part in a federal decision: there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple technical amendment that changes a specific date in a previous act. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. There is no interaction with parties outside the federal government described in this text.
